facts: A multistep problem hides a first unknown side that you must find before the side you actually want.
Find the intermediate side with $h=\sqrt{a^{2}+b^{2}}$ or $a=\sqrt{h^{2}-b^{2}}$, whichever fits.
**Keep the intermediate value exact** — carry a surd such as $\sqrt{52}$ and substitute its square in the next step.
**Round only at the final step**; rounding an intermediate value early makes the final answer inaccurate.
For a perimeter, find every missing side first, then add all the sides.
steps: Round only at the final step.

workedExamples.solution_text:
First find the shared side.
$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{8^{2}+6^{2}}\\y&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
This is a shorter side of the second right-angled triangle.
$\begin{align*}x&=\sqrt{10^{2}+y^{2}}\\x&=\sqrt{10^{2}+10^{2}}\\x&=\sqrt{200}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Find the shared hypotenuse first.
$\begin{align*}x&=\sqrt{6^{2}+8^{2}}\\x&=10\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
The second triangle has hypotenuse $15\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{15^{2}-x^{2}}\\y&=\sqrt{225-100}\\y&=\sqrt{125}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The two end sections of the base are equal.
$\begin{align*}x&=(18-10)\div2\\x&=4\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Use the height and one end section to find a sloping side.
$\begin{align*}y&=\sqrt{4^{2}+7^{2}}\\y&=\sqrt{65}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Keep the sloping length exact until the final calculation.
$\begin{align*}P&=18+10+2\sqrt{65}\\P&\approx44.1\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The horizontal leg of the right-angled triangle is $24-19=5\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}s&=\sqrt{5^{2}+12^{2}}\\s&=13\text{ cm}\\P&=24+19+12+13\\P&=68.0\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

Both halves of the vertical diagonal are $7\text{ cm}$.
$\begin{align*}\text{Left side}&=\sqrt{12^{2}+7^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{193}\text{ cm}\\\text{Right side}&=\sqrt{9^{2}+7^{2}}\\&=\sqrt{130}\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Add both pairs of sides, keeping their lengths exact.
$\begin{align*}P&=2\sqrt{193}+2\sqrt{130}\\P&\approx50.6\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The perpendicular from the centre bisects the water surface, so half its width is $15\text{ cm}$. Let $h$ be the distance from the centre to the surface.
$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{17^{2}-15^{2}}\\h&=\sqrt{64}\\h&=8\text{ cm}\end{align*}$
Subtract this distance from the radius.
$\begin{align*}d&=17-8\\d&=9\text{ cm}\end{align*}$

The perpendicular from the tower bisects the road segment within range. Let $h$ be half this segment.
$\begin{align*}h&=\sqrt{25^{2}-9^{2}}\\h&=\sqrt{544}\text{ km}\end{align*}$
Double the exact intermediate length, then round.
$\begin{align*}x&=2\sqrt{544}\\x&\approx46.65\text{ km}\end{align*}$

The kite has two pairs of equal adjacent sides. Its diagonals meet at right angles, and the horizontal diagonal bisects the vertical diagonal.

development.solution_text:
Each half of the vertical diagonal is $5\text{ cm}$.
Each left side is $\sqrt{12^{2}+5^{2}}=\sqrt{169}=13\text{ cm}$.
Each right side is $\sqrt{9^{2}+5^{2}}=\sqrt{106}\text{ cm}$.
The perimeter adds both pairs of equal sides.
$P=2\times13+2\sqrt{106}$
$\approx46.6\text{ cm}$

A cylindrical pipe of radius $12.5\text{ cm}$ holds water.
The flat surface of the water is $20\text{ cm}$ wide.
Find the depth $d$ of the water.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the intermediate side**
Half the water surface is $10\text{ cm}$, forming a right-angled triangle with the radius.
$\sqrt{12.5^{2}-10^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{56.25}$
$=7.5\text{ cm}$
This is the distance from the centre down to the water surface.
$d=12.5-7.5$
$=5\text{ cm}$

Half the water surface is $12\text{ cm}$, forming a right-angled triangle with the radius.
$\sqrt{13^{2}-12^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{25}$

2. **Find the required side**
The depth is the radius minus the distance from the centre to the water surface.

[/tikz]
A cell tower is $14\text{ km}$ from a straight road and provides signal within a $31\text{ km}$ radius.
Find $x$, the total length of road that lies within signal range.
Round to $2$ decimal places.
mastery.solution_text:
1. **Find the intermediate side**
Half the road length forms a right-angled triangle with the $14\text{ km}$ distance and the $31\text{ km}$ radius.
$\sqrt{31^{2}-14^{2}}$
$=\sqrt{765}$
This is half of $x$, so double it.
$x=2\sqrt{765}$
$\approx55.32\text{ km}$
